Products

Solar Module Mounting Structures

VRM STRUCTURES manufactures hot-dip galvanized and aluminum module mounting structures for solar installations all over the world. Our range covers Metal Roof MMS, RCC Roof MMS, Ground Mounted Solar Structures, Carport MMS, and Customized MMS engineered for unique site requirements. Every structure is built in-house, from steel sourcing to quality-tested Galvanizing, for reliable EPC and rooftop solar projects.

RCC Roof MMS

Robust flat-roof systems with ballasted foundations or anchor-fastened mounts, delivering exceptional wind resistance without damaging RCC waterproofing.

Customized MMS

Tailor-made solar mounting solutions engineered dynamically for complex topographies, specialized angles, and non-standard project geometries.

Aluminum Mounting Structures

Anodized, lightweight, and highly aesthetic aluminum structures optimized for rooftop and high-salinity coastal installations.

Hot Dip Galvanized

Heavy-duty hot-dip galvanized steel structures built to withstand severe wind loads and corrosive outdoor environments.

FRP Walkway

Corrosion-proof Fibreglass Reinforced Plastic walkway panels designed for safe and durable solar rooftop maintenance access.

FRP Handrail

Non-conductive, lightweight, and highly weather-resistant handrail systems ensuring maximum safety across elevated solar plants.

Insights & News

Insights & Updates

Latest articles on solar mounting structures, industry trends, and EPC best practices from the VRM STRUCTURES team.

Engineering

Solar Mounting Structures: Higher Steel Strength Does Not Automatically Mean Less Deflection

Upgrading to a higher steel grade improves resistance to yielding, but it does not make an unchanged purlin stiffer. Here is why strength and stiffness must be checked separately when selecting steel for solar mounting structures.

Velmurugan Rathinam (Founder & Director, VRM Structures)
Engineering

Solar Mounting Structure Support Spacing: Why Purlin Span Matters

Same profile, same thickness, longer span. Moving purlin supports from 2 m to 3 m raises bending demand by 125% and deflection about five times. Why support spacing must be checked alongside the steel section.

Velmurugan Rathinam (Founder & Director, VRM Structures)
Engineering

Solar Mounting Structure Wind Loads: Why Location and Building Height Matter

Same modules, same layout, two rooftops: Bengaluru at 10 m and Chennai at 30 m. Why basic wind speed, building height, terrain and roof position all change the wind-load check for a solar mounting structure.

Velmurugan Rathinam (Founder & Director, VRM Structures)
Support & Help

Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions about our solar mounting structures, manufacturing process, and ordering answered by the VRM STRUCTURES team.

1What type of Solar mounting structures do you offer?

We offer a variety of solar mounting structures, including ground mount systems, rooftop mounts, pole mounts, and non-penetrative roof mounts, designed to meet diverse project needs and site conditions.

2Are your products customisable?

Yes, we provide customised solar racking solutions tailored to your specific project requirements, ensuring optimal performance and compatibility with your unique architectural design.

3What materials are your mounting system made of?

Our mounting systems are constructed from high-quality steel and aluminum, ensuring durability, strength, and resistance to harsh weather conditions.

4Do you provide installation support?

Yes, we offer comprehensive support that includes installation guidelines, technical documentation, and design assistance to ensure your project is successful from start to finish

5What certifications do your products have?

Our products adhere to industry standards and regulations, and we provide Material Test Certificates, load data, and compliance documents to assure you of their quality and reliability.

6How do I determine which mounting solution is right for my project?

Our experienced team is available to assess your project needs, providing recommendations based on factors such as site conditions, energy requirements, and architectural design.
